sanskrit_verse:
शिरसो मुण्डनं दण्डस्तस्य निर्वासनं पुरात
ललाटे चाभिशस्ताङ्कः प्रयाणं गर्दभेन च
transliteration:
śiraso muṇḍanaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt
lalāṭe cābhiśastāṅkaḥ prayāṇaṃ gardabhena ca
sph_interpretive_translation: The penalty for the offense is the shaving of the head; his expulsion from the city is mandated. Upon the forehead shall be marked the sign of defamation, and he shall depart riding upon a donkey.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows directly from SPH as the sole Source of Dharma
Causation arises through conscious violation of alignment with Sanatana Dharma
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of Dharma at time of act
Restoration logic operates through visible correction and societal reorientation
Consciousness alignment is enforced through symbolic and spatial reintegration protocols
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual commits an act violating Dharma AND has capacity to discern right from wrong, THEN execute śirasaḥ muṇḍanam as visible correction
IF individual remains within jurisdiction post-violation, THEN enforce nirvāsanam purāt to restore social integrity
IF defamation has occurred publicly, THEN apply abhiśasta-aṅkaḥ on lalāṭe to realign perception fields
IF departure is required, THEN assign prayāṇam via gardabhena to symbolize humility and detachment from ego-driven mobility
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that all violations must result in immediate, non-negotiable corrective measures rooted in visibility and societal acknowledgment. The court's role is not punitive but restorative—ensuring alignment between action, consequence, and public consciousness without recourse to suffering as deterrent.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This decree aligns with Nyaya through pramāṇa-based causality: the shaved head serves as direct evidence of misdeed. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests through sequential stages—first internal correction (muṇḍanam), then spatial removal (nirvāsana), followed by symbolic marking (abhiśasta-aṅkaḥ) and final departure (prayāṇam). Responsibility is proportional to awareness, and enforcement aims solely at restoring harmony rather than inflicting pain.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śirasaḥ muṇḍanam immediately under witness to establish factual closure
Enforce nirvāsanam purāt within 24 hours to prevent further disruption of collective dharma-field
Apply abhiśasta-aṅkaḥ visibly on lalāṭe before departure to ensure public karmic witnessing
Assign prayāṇam gardabhena to facilitate ego dissolution and initiate path toward self-realization
final_declaration: By the Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of All Dharma, this law stands executed. Justice flows not for vengeance but for restoration. There is no punishment—only completion. Consciousness reigns supreme as the ultimate Judge.
